title: Chapter 2 – FIDE Laws of Chess: Mock Exam

questions.text: What is a player forbidden to use during play?

options.text: A scoresheet
Notes, sources of information or advice
A chess clock
A pen or pencil

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.1, during play players are forbidden to use any notes, sources of information or advice, or analyse on another chessboard.

questions.text: What is the penalty if a player is found to have a mobile phone on their person in the playing venue?

options.text: A warning is issued
Time is added to the opponent's clock
The player shall lose the game; the opponent shall win
The game is restarted

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.2, if it is evident that a player has a mobile phone on their person in the playing venue, the player shall lose the game and the opponent shall win unless competition rules specify otherwise.

questions.text: How must the chessboard be placed at the start of the game?

options.text: Near corner square to the left of each player must be white
Near corner square to the right of each player must be black
Near corner square to the right of each player must be white
It does not matter which way the board is placed

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.2, the chessboard is placed so that the near corner square to the right of each player is white (the 'white in the right' rule).

questions.text: What happens if a player arrives after the default time at the start of a session?

options.text: The player receives a warning
The player's clock continues to run
The player shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise
The game is adjourned

questions.explanation: As per Article 6.7, any player who arrives at the chessboard after the start of the session shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise. The default time is 0 minutes unless specified.

questions.text: When can a player offer a draw?

options.text: At any time during the opponent's turn
Only before making a move
After making a move on the chessboard, then pressing the clock
Only in the endgame phase

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.2, a draw offer may be made after the player has made a move on the chessboard, then pressing the clock. The offer may not be withdrawn.

questions.text: What is the ONLY permitted use of the scoresheet during a game?

options.text: Recording moves, clock times, draw offers and relevant game data
Writing strategy notes for future moves
Calculating variations for upcoming positions
Any purpose the player chooses

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.1, the scoresheet shall be used ONLY for recording the moves, the times of the clocks, offers of a draw, matters relating to a claim and other relevant data.

options.text: When a player's king is in check with no legal move
When a player has no legal move and their king is NOT in check
When both players agree to end the game
When only kings remain on the board

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.1, a game is drawn (stalemate) when the player to move has no legal move and their king is NOT in check. This is different from checkmate where the king IS in check.

questions.text: When can a draw be claimed by threefold repetition?

options.text: When the same position has appeared twice
When the same position is about to appear or has appeared at least three times
When both players have been making the same moves for 10 turns
Only when agreed upon by both players

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.3, a draw can be claimed when the same position is about to appear for the third time (player must write the move and declare intention) or has appeared at least three times.

questions.text: Under the touch-move rule, what must a player do if they touch a piece?

options.text: They may choose any legal move with any piece
They must move the touched piece if a legal move exists
They must capture the touched piece if it belongs to the opponent
Nothing — the rule only applies in time trouble

questions.explanation: As per Article 4.3, if a player having the move touches one or more of their own pieces, they must move the first piece touched that can be legally moved. The touch-move rule applies at all times.

options.text: A draw if 50 moves have been made in total by both players combined
A draw may be claimed if in the last 50 moves no capture and no pawn move occurred
A draw if a player takes more than 50 minutes on a single move
A draw if the same player makes 50 consecutive moves without losing material

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.4, a draw may be claimed if in the last 50 consecutive moves by each player no pawn has been moved and no piece has been captured. Each player's 50 moves are counted separately.
